body.statement:
For the saturated likelihood-ratio domain \(\mathcal V_P\), the full fixed-defect separated stratum \(\mathcal U_P\), and the actual path class in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\), does every \(s\in\mathcal C_P^\perp\) lie in the \(L^2(P)\)-closure of finite linear combinations of scores of admissible DQM paths, including at intersections with moving kernels and a shared \((W,X)\) marginal? Equivalently, does
\[
\mathcal T_P=\mathcal C_P^\perp
\]
hold on every such joint solvability germ?  Neither equality nor bridge-solvability path realization is included in the chart definition.
body.justification: This remains the reverse-inclusion problem for the full saturated fixed-defect intersection, not for an analyst-selected subchart.
body.gap: The finite constant-rank and branch calculations do not provide a general coupled Hilbert-space incidence chart, and operator continuity alone supplies no differentiable path lift.
body.consumer: Its resolution determines whether the affine projection is the information bound throughout the unrestricted joint model.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct actual DQM paths whose score span is the full annihilator of the three normal classes on the unrestricted saturated fixed-defect joint-solvability germ, or exhibit a counterexample inside that same full germ.
obligation.obstruction: The declared closed-range and operator-continuity conditions yield continuous moving kernel and cokernel projections but neither differentiable projection lifts nor a locally surjective constant-rank parameterization of the intersection of the outcome- and treatment-solvability loci. First-order annihilation therefore does not by itself integrate to an admissible path.
obligation.attempted: I reduced the proposed lifting argument to a constant-rank parameterization of the coupled incidence set and checked what the operator perturbation lemma actually supplies along DQM paths. Its conclusion is only continuity with an unspecified modulus, so the needed derivative cannot be inferred. The regular finite chart, singular two-branch chart, and transverse different-row-space chart remain valid positive tests, but none supplies the missing unrestricted Hilbert parameterization.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved finite-dimensional calculations establish reverse lifting on three strictly positive germs: the regular \(36\)-cell rank-two germ, the singular two-branch \(3\)-by-\(3\) germ, and the transverse \(4\)-by-\(4\) rank-two germ with different arm row spaces. They also establish that an arbitrary singleton subchart has tangent space \(\{0\}\), so chart saturation is necessary.

For the general germ, the available operator argument stops strictly before path realization. Indeed, along a DQM path \(P_t\), DQM gives \(H(P_t,P)=O(|t|)\). The transported-operator continuity assumption and the kernel perturbation lemma imply only
\[
\left\|\widetilde\Pi_{N,a}(P_t)-\widetilde\Pi_{N,a}(P)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\vee
\left\|\widetilde\Pi_{K,a}(P_t)-\widetilde\Pi_{K,a}(P)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=o(1).
\]
No declared assumption supplies an \(O(|t|)\) modulus, a derivative of either projection, or a locally surjective constant-rank parameterization of the intersection
\[
\mathcal U_P\cap\mathcal L_{\mathrm{out}}(P)\cap
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{trt}}(P).
\]
Consequently, annihilation of the three displayed first-order normal classes cannot presently be integrated into an actual curve in that intersection. The finite incidence parameterizations prove the desired equality on their stated finite germs, but do not imply the unrestricted Hilbert-space equality.
